Route A expands at \(2.00\times10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\); route B expands at \(1.00\times10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\). Compare the work done.
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Equilibrium, State Functions, and Thermodynamic Paths under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
For each horizontal part of the graph, the area is pressure multiplied by the volume change. The volume change is \(2.00\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}\). Therefore \[W_A=(2.00\times10^5)(2.00\times10^{-3})=400\,\mathrm J,\] \[W_B=(1.00\times10^5)(2.00\times10^{-3})=200\,\mathrm J.\] The vertical parts have no volume change, so they do no boundary work. Final result: route A gives \(400\,\mathrm J\), while route B gives \(200\,\mathrm J\).

Final answer:
Route A gives \(400\,\mathrm J\), while route B gives \(200\,\mathrm J\).

Check:
The conclusion agrees with both the defining relation and the relevant limiting or qualitative behaviour of the model.

What must be zero, and what may be non-zero?
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Equilibrium, State Functions, and Thermodynamic Paths under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
The start and finish are the same state, so every state-function change is zero. In particular, \(\Delta p=\Delta V=\Delta T=\Delta U=0\). All state-function changes are zero, but the total heat and work need not be zero individually.
